results.claim: At the advertised knight-encounter staging configuration, the idealized ambiguous move has the two global possibilities ±r, and both stated branches are exclusive and end in K(q+r;a,r,f).
results.proof_sketch: Let (T,H,B)=(q+r,q+2r,q+2r+f), with a,r,f orthogonal signed unit vectors, and define K(p;a,r,f)={p,p+a,p+2r+f}. Among the 48 signed-coordinate transformations, those fixing the colored-neighbor direction −f and wall direction −a form a two-element stabilizer whose orbit on r is {r,−r}. First H enters B's old node while B moves to q+r+f or q+3r+f. In the −r branch, the next round sends T to q+r+a, B to q+r, and H to q+3r+f. In the +r branch, H first moves to q+r+f; the following round sends H to q+r and T to q+r+a while B remains at q+3r+f. Both endpoints are {q+r,q+r+a,q+3r+f}=K(q+r;a,r,f). Exact enumeration found only unit or idle moves, distinct same-round destinations, and no oppositely traversed edge. This proves only the idealized positional macro.

results.claim: From the advertised ordinary-transition staging configuration, the distinct-choice branch gives D(q;d,e,f), while the contact-and-rotation branch gives D(q;e,d,f), without a collision or edge swap.
results.proof_sketch: Let d and e be the two distinct directions in {a,−r}, define D(p;u,v,w)={p,p+u,p+v+w}, and start from {q,q+d,q+f}. In the distinct-choice branch, the third robot moves from q+f to q+e+f, giving D(q;d,e,f). In the contact branch, it first reaches q+d+f. The stated rotation then moves the occupants of q and q+d to q+e and q, respectively, giving {q,q+e,q+d+f}=D(q;e,d,f). Orthogonality makes every indicated non-idle displacement a unit grid edge. The destinations are distinct, and the rotation edges q→q+e and q+d→q are neither equal nor oppositely oriented copies of one edge. This proves only the positional branch effects, not their reachability or realization by colored local-view rules.

results.claim: From the advertised outer-reset conversion staging configuration, every choice of d, x and the ±d conversion branch is exclusive and ends in K(s;y,d,x).
results.proof_sketch: Let h=−f; choose d from {a,−r}, let e be the other direction, choose x from {e,h}, and let y be the other member of {e,h}. After the advertised follower shift, label the positions s, s+d, and s+d+x by L, M, and C. The conversion moves M to C's old position and C by ±d. In the +d branch, correcting M to s+x gives {s,s+x,s+2d+x}. In the −d branch, correcting M to s+2d+x gives the same set, although C rather than M then occupies s+x. Finally, send whichever robot occupies s+x to s while L moves from s to s+y. The endpoint is {s,s+y,s+2d+x}=K(s;y,d,x). Exact enumeration over every advertised choice found only unit or idle displacements, distinct same-round destinations, and no edge swap. This remains an unlabeled positional lemma and establishes no compatible shade transitions.

results.claim: The three retained positional macros do not define or prove a visibility-one algorithm with at most 76 shades.
results.proof_sketch: The source requires an algorithm A=(Cl,Init,T), where Cl is a finite shade set, Init maps every eligible grid to a nonempty set of initial configurations, and T maps every local view to a movement and next shade. The retained lemmas describe only finitely many uncolored geometric branches from assumed staging configurations. They specify neither Cl nor Init nor T, and they do not prove consistency on local-view orbits, reachability of the staging configurations, termination under every adversarial transformation sequence, preservation of global invariants, or perpetual coverage of every eligible grid. Hence they are only conditional positional calculations, not an at-most-76-shade construction or a demonstrated step toward one.

results.claim: If a visibility-one algorithm for exactly three Batdroids without common chirality solves PEP, then on every N×N×N cave with even N≥14, every permitted execution has infinitely many rounds in which some Batdroid's current rule admits more than one global destination.
results.proof_sketch: Call a round unambiguous when every Batdroid's global destination is invariant under every indistinguishable transformation of its current view. Suppose a PEP execution had an all-unambiguous suffix beginning at time τ. The even cube has more than three centers, so choose a center c empty at τ and let t>τ be its first later occupation, which PEP guarantees. Its entrant B1 came from a neighbor. B1 was not lost at t−1: a lost view is fixed by all signed-coordinate transformations, and any non-idle unit direction has all six unit directions in its orbit, making the move ambiguous. Thus another Batdroid was adjacent to B1 at t−1. The source's center-case argument now applies to this realized suffix. At t, either one Batdroid neighbors both others, trapping all three in a central slice; B1 is paired and the third is isolated, trapping the pair on a line until the central-slice case occurs; B1 is isolated while the other two are paired, fixing B1 at c and trapping the pair on a line until a preceding case occurs; or all three are isolated and become idle after any wall-neighbor moves away and becomes lost. Each confines the tail to a proper subset of the cube, contradicting PEP. Hence no ambiguity-free suffix exists, so ambiguous rounds occur infinitely often. This rules out using ambiguity only for a finite initialization or one-time orientation choice.

results.claim: The recurrent-ambiguity obstruction is shade-blind and does not provide a lower bound separating 76 shades from 77.
results.proof_sketch: The argument uses positions, walls, visibility, and transformation stabilizers but never compares shades or counts color states. Recurrent ambiguity is compatible in principle with every nonempty shade set, and ambiguity is expressly permitted by the target. The boundary is also limited: N=14 is the smallest even side satisfying the source proof's assumptions N≥13 and even. On an odd cube there is only one center, so the empty-center pigeonhole step can fail; the sealed source does not certify the argument for smaller even cubes or rectangular grids. Thus the result is a precise necessary condition for a solution, not a shade-count lower bound.

results.claim: Neither alternative in the target is established.
results.proof_sketch: The construction alternative requires an actual ambiguous visibility-one tuple (Cl,Init,T) for exactly three Batdroids using at most 76 shades, together with a proof that every permitted execution perpetually visits every vertex of every grid whose side lengths are at least four. The preceding insufficiency result shows that no such construction is supplied. The optimality alternative requires a lower bound excluding every algorithm using at most 76 shades; no retained result supplies such a bound. Therefore neither target alternative is established.

final_writeup:
Revision outcome: the open target remains unresolved, but the independently audited recurrent-ambiguity theorem is valid partial progress. Accordingly, claimed_resolution is PARTIAL; this does not assert that either requested alternative has been established.

The three audited coordinate macros are retained exactly. At their advertised staging configurations, their stated branches and endpoints are correct and exclusive. They remain conditional, uncolored positional calculations: they supply no shade set, initialization map, total local-view transition function, reachability or composition invariant, adversarial convergence proof, or perpetual-coverage proof. Consequently they do not establish an algorithm using at most 76 shades.

The prescribed structural-reformulation lens was tested against the available route of identifying shade states and quotienting the 77-shade dynamics while preserving every local-view transition, initialization, and adversarial branch. The sealed source text omits the rule tables needed to test such a congruence, while the retained macros contain no shade transitions. Therefore no concrete state identification or conclusion-transfer proof can be certified. A generic quotient restatement alone would neither construct a 76-shade solver nor exclude all such solvers, so it yields no material change to the seven audited claim/proof pairs.

The obstruction does yield one precise necessary condition. Consider any purported solution on an even N×N×N cube with N≥14. If one of its executions had only finitely many ambiguous rounds, choose a time after the last one. More than three central vertices exist, so some center is then empty; PEP requires its later occupation. From that first later center visit, the source's four-case argument needs only that the realized suffix be unambiguous. It forces the Batdroids into a central slice, a line together with an isolated stationary Batdroid, or an all-idle configuration, contradicting PEP. Thus every execution of any solution must invoke an ambiguous rule infinitely often. In particular, ambiguity cannot be confined to initialization or used once to choose an orientation followed by a deterministic patrol.

This obstruction is independent of shades. It requires recurrent ambiguity but rules out no particular positive shade count, including counts at most 76. Its certified boundary is the source proof's even-cube family N≥14; the center argument does not, from the sealed evidence alone, extend to odd cubes, smaller even cubes, or all rectangular grids.

Accordingly, the constructive alternative remains unsupported, and no universal lower bound excludes all ambiguous algorithms with at most 76 shades. The source's impossibility theorem for well-defined algorithms cannot prove 77 optimal because the target expressly permits ambiguity. Neither target alternative is established; PARTIAL records only the independently verified necessary condition and positional lemmas.
